Effects of Structure and Hydrodynamics on the Sooting Behavior of Spherical Microgravity Diffusion Flames

key_findings: Soot formation requires a region where local C/O ratio and T exceed their critical values, and where strain rate is sufficiently low.
Microgravity spherical diffusion flames extinguish when the peak temperature first decreases below 1130 K.
Steady-state spherical diffusion flames are possible.
fields.earth_applications: This project has the potential for improving efficiency and reducing pollutant emissions in terrestrial combustors.

paper_findings.text: Extinction temperature is nearly invariant with flow rate, around 1100 K for oxygen into 4% ethylene flames.
Extinction begins when the flame radius starts to decrease.
Base extinction often led to complete extinction, where all flame luminosity disappeared during a drop test.
Microgravity laminar flames are sensitive to hydrodynamic disturbances.
The flames were ignited immediately after release into microgravity using a spring-loaded wire.
The serial pair of solenoid valves facilitated smooth ignition via optimization of the initial gas discharge.
